title: Classic mistakes: keys in the code, rolling your own algorithm and nonce reuse

videos.script: Sixteen lessons have explained algorithms that are, as far as anybody knows, unbroken. AES, elliptic curves, SHA-256, Argon2. Systems still lose their data. {{title}} When they do, the mathematics is almost never what failed. What fails is the way someone used it, and three of those ways turn up again and again. {{three}} The first is a key written into the code, where everybody who can read the repository can read the key, for as long as the repository exists. {{key}} The second is a cipher somebody built themselves, which looks fine and passes every test they thought of. {{homemade}} The third is a nonce used twice, one repeated number that undoes the encryption it was meant to protect. {{nonce}} This lesson shows each of them in the lab, how to find it in a system you look after, and what to do on the day you do.
